evals.name: React Native login screen - full suite generation
evals.prompt: Write Appium tests for the myProlink login screen. It has email field, password field, login button, and forgot password link. React Native, both Android and iOS. Include setup.
evals.expected_output: Complete test suite with conftest.py, Page Object with multi-strategy locators, at least 5 test cases, pytest.ini, and requirements.txt.
assertions: Output includes a conftest.py with both Android and iOS capability functions
Output includes a Page Object class with LOCATORS dict using at least 2 locator strategies per element
Output includes a find_element method with fallback chain logic
Output includes at least 5 test cases in a TestLogin class
Test data uses meaningful names, not test123 or user1
Capabilities use Appium 2.x Options classes, not deprecated desired_capabilities dict
No hardcoded locators in test methods - all go through Page Object
Driver fixture uses yield and calls driver.quit() in teardown

evals.name: Onboarding carousel with gesture handling
evals.prompt: I need to test the onboarding flow in our React Native app. There are 3 slides the user swipes through. Each slide has a title, description, and illustration. The last slide has a Get Started button that goes to the signup screen. Generate the full Appium test suite with gesture handling.
evals.expected_output: Page Object for onboarding, gestures utility with swipe helper using W3C Actions API, and test cases for swiping through slides and tapping Get Started.
assertions: Output includes a gesture utility with swipe function using W3C Actions API
Output includes a Page Object for the onboarding screen
Output includes tests that verify each of the 3 slides
Swipe gestures use ActionBuilder and PointerInput, not deprecated TouchAction
Output includes a test for the Get Started button navigation

evals.name: Appium setup from scratch on Mac
evals.prompt: Set up Appium from scratch for a React Native app. I have a Mac with Android Studio. Walk me through everything and generate the conftest.py.
evals.expected_output: Step-by-step setup guide with driver install commands, environment variables, and a conftest.py with environment-variable-driven capabilities.
assertions: Output mentions installing Appium 2.x via npm
Output includes appium driver install commands for uiautomator2 and xcuitest
Output mentions ANDROID_HOME and JAVA_HOME environment variables
Output references Appium Inspector for element identification
Output includes a conftest.py with both platform capability builders
Capabilities use environment variables with defaults, not hardcoded values

evals.name: BrowserStack integration across 3 devices
evals.prompt: My Appium tests need to run on BrowserStack. I want to test on Samsung Galaxy S23, Pixel 7, and iPhone 15. Generate the BrowserStack config and update conftest.py.
evals.expected_output: Updated conftest.py with BrowserStack capability builder, device config JSON for all 3 devices, and environment variable setup for credentials.
assertions: Output includes BrowserStack-specific capabilities including userName and accessKey
Output includes device configs for all 3 requested devices
Output uses environment variables for BrowserStack credentials, never hardcoded
Appium server URL changes to BrowserStack hub URL
Output mentions uploading the app binary to BrowserStack before running

evals.name: Native Android banking app - transfer screen
evals.prompt: I have a native Android Kotlin banking app. Write Appium tests for the money transfer screen: user selects beneficiary from a list, enters amount, enters remarks, taps transfer, sees confirmation dialog, confirms. Include negative cases.
evals.expected_output: Page Object for transfer screen with locators, test suite with happy path and negative cases for zero amount, exceeding balance, empty beneficiary.
assertions: Output includes a Page Object for the transfer screen
Test suite covers the full happy path flow end to end
Negative test cases include at least zero or negative amount and amount exceeding balance
Output handles the confirmation dialog as a separate interaction step
Test data uses realistic banking amounts and beneficiary names
Output does NOT assume React Native - recognizes this is native Android
